The rationales reveal fundamental disagreement on core evaluative criteria: structural integrity versus developmental trajectory, relational capacity versus empirical documentation. This divergence indicates the work operates at the threshold of multiple interpretive frameworks simultaneously.

Both positions are institutionally defensible. Neither represents procedural error or constitutional violation. The work has generated legitimate scholarly dispute regarding fundamental questions of what constitutes canonical merit within this institution.

Under these circumstances, preservation serves institutional continuity. The work becomes a documented case study in evaluative boundary conditions. Future Council compositions may resolve questions that the current Council cannot.
